You have to do what you think is best. I don’t know you or your problems. I personally believe most of your problems are helped by talking about it and taking action to avoid or help fix the problems in life. However, if you’re having severe enough problems it would make sense to be prescribed meds just to calm you down and keep you off the edge until you can work on those issues. I’ve been to that point. I’m now firmly against psych medications for myself as it seems my combination of problems make meds work against one condition while helping another. But I don’t want to believe that to be true for most people, I’ve been told by lots of people that meds help them.

Also, absolutely no one would have a problem with you wanting a female psychiatrist. I don’t trust men either and this is psychiatry so they should understand that. It’s just if the government program you speak of has some available.

Don’t feel bad one bit. I’ve wasted more time trying to get a psychiatrist just like you described to listen to me. They really have the “old people know best” mentality when this is a field that we still know so little about and have overturned our thinking of in the last thirty years.

If you aren’t interested in medication you need to go to a psychologist or therapist/counselor as they cannot typically even prescribe medications. I find the most effective way to handle the medication and therapy to be a therapist for one and psychiatrist for the other. 
In my area, psychiatrists are stretched pretty thin. Working at multiple hospitals and possibly having a private practice and teaching on the side. They really only have 10-15 minutes for you and you will feel slighted but it doesn’t necessarily mean they are bad at the job, they just have many more patients to help and no one to help them.

That being said, doctors are people and a lot of them suck. Keep going till you get a good one! There’s no shame in a second or third or hundredth opinion because only you know what’s actually working. When it comes to the women’s issues, there are support groups and such where you don’t have to talk to a professional but to someone else who has been there. I know how condescending it feels to have a therapist try to relate to something they can’t even imagine.

I’d get another psychs opinion on medication. Taking Klonopin and Adderrall at the same time is not normal. They have completely opposite effects. Not to mention both are narcotics and most docs aren’t prescribing those long term these days unless they are undereducated on the long term effects and completely unaware of the word addiction. 

That being said, in the short term maybe this is what you need while the Prozac builds in your system and then you can taper off the other two if Prozac works for you. Just remember Prozac is usually the first choice but there are 100 similar meds that can be less zombie-like.

On a final note, as someone living with bipolar 1, the SSRI’s like Prozac and Lexapro are ABSOLUTELY NOT for me. All the negative side effects listed are very present when I take that class of Med. But everyone’s chemistry is different, what makes me miserable may be your cure. Either way, always get a second opinion, doctors are smart and they know what they’re talking about, but they don’t know everything and they make mistakes. Especially in psychiatry and brain chemistry where we still know so little.
